# Demo 1
D1=[[0]*6,[6]*6,[1]*6,[3]*6,[1]*6,[7]*6]
E1=[[7]*6,[6]*6,[1]*6,[3]*6,[1]*6,[7]*6]
print('demo1',transform(D1)==E1)
# Demo 2: draw the observed down-right diagonal runs.
def draw(n, runs):
    g=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    for color,offset,rlo,rhi,orientation in runs:
        for r in range(rlo,rhi+1):
            c=offset+r if orientation=='diff' else offset-r
            if 0<=c<n: g[r][c]=color
    return g
D2=draw(26,[(7,1,0,24,'diff'),(1,4,0,21,'diff'),(9,6,0,19,'diff'),(2,21,0,4,'diff'),(5,24,0,1,'diff'),(3,-16,16,25,'diff'),(3,-19,19,25,'diff')])

E2=[[seq2[(c-r)%7] for c in range(26)] for r in range(26)]
print('demo2',transform(D2)==E2, 'nonzero',sum(v!=0 for row in D2 for v in row))
# Demo 3: draw down-left diagonals with constant row+column.
D3=draw(22,[(9,8,0,8,'sum'),(7,14,0,14,'sum'),(8,23,2,21,'sum'),(5,37,16,21,'sum')])
seq3=[9,5,7,8]

print('demo3',transform(D3)==E3, 'nonzero',sum(v!=0 for row in D3 for v in row))
# Test input mapping is the period-4 down-right sequence.
